title: Pompey the Great
objective: After this level you can describe Pompey’s rise and his conquests in the East.
summary: Pompey rose under Sulla, won huge commands, swept the pirates from the sea in 67 BCE and remade the East. He called himself Magnus.

cards.headline: He called himself “the Great” before most Romans agreed he was.
A general of special commands
cards.body: Pompey first rose to fame as a young commander fighting for Sulla. Later the Roman people voted him extraordinary commands that gave him power over huge areas for years at a time. In 67 BCE he cleared the Mediterranean of pirates in about three months.

cards.headline: Remaking the East
cards.body: Pompey then defeated King Mithridates and reorganized the eastern Mediterranean. He made Syria a Roman province and captured Jerusalem in 63 BCE. He took the name Magnus, “the Great,” in imitation of Alexander the Great.

cards.fact: Pompey swept the pirates from the Mediterranean in about three months.
cards.context: The campaign of 67 BCE was one of the extraordinary commands the Roman people voted him, and its speed made him a hero.

questions.prompt: What name did Pompey take for himself?

options.label: Augustus
options.rationale: That came later, with someone else.

questions.explanation: Pompey called himself Magnus, imitating Alexander the Great.

questions.prompt: Why did Pompey’s commands worry many senators?

options.label: They gave one man vast power for years
They cost Rome its eastern provinces
They were won by bribing the Vestals
They put Carthage back in power

questions.explanation: Extraordinary commands concentrated power in one man, the very thing the Republic was built to prevent.
